text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert INC-2805: increased 502/504s from us-west-2 origins for /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Triggered at 2026-10-09T21:40:01Z. Pager: Maya. Links: https://pd/redwood/INC-2805

Maya: Ack. I'm oncall and jumping in. Dashboard shows global error spike with concentration on us-west-2 POPs. Edge logs show upstream 502s and timeouts to us-west origin pool. No recent deploys.

Maya: Quick notes:
- Edge error rate: 6.5% global, 14% in us-west-2 POPs
- Backend pod restarts in us-west-2a and 2b
- Route53 health checks flapping for several origin IPs

Theo (NetOps): Joining. Cloud console indicates inter-AZ packet loss in us-west-2 starting ~21:37Z, primarily affecting ENIs on a subset of hosts. AWS status: investigating fabric.

Rina (SRE): Seeing weirdness on route preference at edge. Some POPs still route to us-west-2 origins despite weight-based shift started by autoscaler. Suspect route cache / BGP sticky state at edge.

Raj (Eng): Can you paste a sample request id? I'll tail origin logs.

Maya: Sample req ids: r=5f9c1a, r=5f9c4d, r=5f9c8f
Edge excerpt:
```
[2026-10-09T21:41:15Z] edge-pop-chi -> origin us-west-2: upstream response timeout (request_id=5f9c1a)
[2026-10-09T21:41:17Z] edge-pop-lax -> origin us-west-2: 502 Bad Gateway (request_id=5f9c4d)
```

Raj: Origin logs show timeouts during KV cache sync and occasional OOM restarts on a couple of gpu nodes. But majority of errors correlate with network errors from the cloud.

NetBot: autoscaler: Detected health degradation in us-west-2 pool. Initiating cross-region spillover to us-east-1 per policy. Proposed shift: 25%.

Maya: 25% is below our usual urgent threshold. Given the route cache staleness, I'd rather do 35% to start, watch, then escalate. Notify support.

Support-Liu: Notifying CS; compiling list of customers with traffic concentrated in us-west-2. So far 3 high-throughput accounts impacted. Drafting customer note.

Theo: Approve. I'll also run a soft route cache flush on edge POPs that still prefer us-west-2. But caution: full flush causes short lat spikes.

Maya: Let's do staged: 35% shift, edge flush for affected POPs only. Raj, please prepare traffic-shift command and health-check script.

Raj: Running:
```
infractl traffic-shift --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --percent 35 --reason "us-west fabric loss" --watch 120
```

incident-bot: Traffic-shift request recorded; policy requires two approvers for >30% shift. Waiting for Theo approval.

Theo: Approve. Proceed.

~21:44Z Maya: Shift started. Observability shows error-rate drop in POPs that accepted shift. But 4 POPs still showing ~8% errors due to stale route table entries.

Raj: Flushing route cache on specific POPs:
```
edgectl flush-routes --pop lax,sfo,chi --filter origin=us-west-2 --soft
```

NetBot: edgectl operation executed. Soft flush in progress (ETA 18s).

~21:46Z Rina: After flush, most POPs now show requests routing to us-east-1. Error rate down to 1.1%. A handful of long-lived TCP sessions still hitting drained origins and failing (sticky LB sessions).

Maya: Those sticky sessions are likely from older edge proxies with sticky persistence. We should drain by connection ID for those origins to avoid tearing sessions globally. Raj, can you drain the specific origin pool members gracefully?

Raj: Draining insts: inst-0c3f7a, inst-0c3f7b, inst-0c3f8d
Command:
```
./ops/drain-node --region us-west-2 --node inst-0c3f7a,inst-0c3f7b,inst-0c3f8d --grace 120
```

Theo: Also adding temporary autoscaler tag `no-scale-INC-2805` to avoid immediate replacements until AWS signals stable.

NetBot: Tag applied to ASG us-west-2-serving.

~21:50Z Maya: Health good at 35% shift. Error rate fell below 1% globally. Latency stable. Support-Liu: customer notes sent.

Support-Liu: Sent. CS acknowledged. Marking SEV-2 and notifying top-tier customers with mitigation summary.

Maya: AWS says fabric shows intermittent improvement but still elevated packet loss in 2b. Recommend progressive move to 75% then 100% if stable for 5m. Rina, any objections?

Rina: No objections. But add a step: after route cache flush, do a soft TCP RST for lingering sessions to accelerate cutover if error counts don't drop.

Raj: Bumping to 75% now with approvals (Maya, Theo). Running:
```
infractl traffic-shift --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --percent 75 --approve-by Maya,Theo --watch 300
```

incident-bot: Shift to 75% in progress.

~21:56Z Rina: After 75% shift, error rate trending <0.3%. A few enterprise tenants with regional pinning saw transient failures; support added mitigation steps.

Maya: Proceed to 100% in 3m if stable. Also schedule rejoin plan: keep no-scale tag, wait for AWS confirmation, then reintroduce capacity gradually and monitor route propagation.

Raj: Final shift:
```
infractl traffic-shift --from us-west-2 --to us-east-1 --percent 100 --approve-by Maya,Theo,Raj --reason "complete regional failover due to AZ fabric instability"
```

incident-bot: Shift completed at 2026-10-09T21:59:40Z. All new traffic routing to us-east-1. Incident state: mitigated (traffic shifted). SEV-2. Links: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/INC-2805

Theo: AWS ticket created and linked. Will keep monitoring and request RCA.

Maya: Handoff: Rina will watch overnight for any route cache residue and sticky-session replays. I'm off in 25m. Rina, please update runbook with notes about selective POP flush and approvals to reduce friction next time.

Rina: Will do. Adding a checklist: identify affected POPs via route-pref metric, soft flush, staged shift thresholds (35/75/100), drain nodes with grace, tag ASG no-scale, confirm AWS fix, then rejoin.

Support-Liu: Final customer update sent. Will coordinate follow-up postmortem with SEs.

Maya: Thanks team. Closing command: mark INC-2805 mitigated and assign postmortem owner.
